title: Optimal private selection using only Laplace queries
formal: Let $Y$ be a finite set of candidates, each with a public loss function $\ell_y$ of sensitivity one under a one-record database change. To access the database, an algorithm makes $k$ adaptive sensitivity-1 queries. Its answers are $q_i(X)+\mathrm{Lap}(k)$, where $k$ is the scale. Can it guarantee expected excess loss $O(\log|Y|)$ for arbitrary losses? The algorithm may choose the number of queries.
context:
This model corresponds to basic composition for pure privacy. The stronger concentration of Gaussian noise cannot simply be transferred.

Here the menu of candidates is finite and each loss changes by at most one when one database record changes. The algorithm tries to choose a candidate whose expected loss is close to the best available loss. Its only observations are sensitivity-bounded statistical queries with Laplace noise.

Taking more queries is not free in this interface: the noise scale of each answer grows with the total query count k. A method that estimates all losses can spend too much accuracy on candidates that will never be selected. A method that repeatedly eliminates candidates risks making irreversible choices from noisy comparisons. The problem asks whether a carefully organized query process can still reach logarithmic excess loss.
why: The cost of pure privacy is a structural model distinction, rather than an arbitrary change of constants. It determines the reach of noise addition as a universal primitive.

progress.text: The authors explain why their nearly optimal Gaussian method does not yield a tight Laplace bound and leave this model open.

answer_criterion: Construct a query-only algorithm with the displayed expected-loss guarantee for every finite loss family, or prove that no universal constant in that guarantee is possible. Allowing another way to read the database changes the problem.
definitions: The algorithm chooses a finite positive integer k from public information before reading any answers. Each noise draw is independent with density exp(-|z|/k)/(2k). Query choices may depend on earlier answers. The expectation includes oracle and algorithm randomness; the hidden constant is independent of the candidate set and losses. No computation-time bound is imposed.

importance.reason: Determines the limits of the pure-private Laplace query interface, isolating what stronger mechanisms would have to add.
